newsitem.title: USA: Dow jumps 47 points to set 19th record this year.
newsitem.headline: Dow jumps 47 points to set 19th record this year.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average set its 19th record close of the year Thursday on a late burst of buying after blue-chip stocks overcame a bigger-than-expected rise in consumer prices last month.
The Dow ended up 47.39 points at 7,333.55 -- its first close above 7,300 -- as it eclipsed Monday's record finish of 7,292.75.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,280 to 1,165 on moderate volume of 458 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks also set a record, rising 5.84 points to 841.88.

Blue-chip stocks had been stuck in a narrow trading range for most of the session as mixed inflation signals prompted some investors to stay on the sidelines prior to the Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting next Tuesday.
Conflicting economic news has sent mixed signals as to whether the Fed would raise interest rates next week.

"We see a 50/50 chance that the Fed may raise rates just to continue with their pre-emptive strike but the inflation numbers have looked pretty good this week," said Elaine Garzarelli, who remains bullish with a year-end target of 7,600 for the Dow.

Financial markets fell initially after the government reported that the core rate of inflation, which excludes the volatile food and energy sectors, in the Consumer Price Index rose 0.3 percent, which exceeded Wall Street's forecasts.
The overall CPI was up 0.1 percent last month, matching the 0.1 percent rise in March.
Economists had predicted the overall index would rise by 0.1 percent, and they expected the core rate to climb by just 0.2 percent.
Industrial production was unchanged, compared with economists' forecast for a rise of 0.2 percent, and capacity utilization was 83.4 percent, against a forecast of 84.1 percent.

The retail inflation data came one day after the government reported surprisingly good news on wholesale prices, as the Producer Price Index for April posted its biggest drop in nearly four years, falling 0.6 percent.
Traders said they also were waiting to see if there would be a new round of fresh investment money pouring into in mutual funds.
AMG Data Services and Mutual Fund Trim Tabs, two firms that track mutual funds, are expected to release their numbers this week on cash flowing into mutual funds.
Technology stocks sizzled throughout the session, powered by renewed interest in the sector and gains in computer disk drive makers.
Internet bookseller Amazon.com Inc. soared 60 percent in its initial public offering to 30 but settled back to close up 5-1/2 to 23-1/2.

Computer disk drive makers Western Digital Corp. jumped 2-7/8 to 66-5/8, Quantum Corp. rose 3-3/4 to 47-1/2 and Seagate Technology Inc. was up 1-3/8 at 49-7/8 after Lehman Brothers raised its opinion of the sector.
The most-heavily traded Nasdaq stock was Informix Corp., which rose 2-3/16 to 11-3/8 on takeover rumours.
Gateway 2000 surged 5-1/2 to 67 after it set a stock split and said it would buy back up to 10 million of its shares.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 18.03 points to 1,353.58. The American Stock Exchange index rose 1.50 to 583.47.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 2.05 to 437.65. The average share was up 20 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,924.245, up 49.682 or 0.63 percent.
